title: Power Pages: first-class support for Power Platform connector APIs
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and corrected endpoint-filtering route are supported, and the gaps are appropriately limited to the planned native connector capability. Minor corrections should reflect the published product-level licensing, extend the connector-policy route, and cite the documentation supporting policy creation with connector classifications.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans native Power Platform connector support in Power Pages.
claims.quote: Native connectors support through Power Pages will allow organizations to securely connect their websites/portals directly to enterprise systems

claims.claim: The roadmap names SQL, SAP and Oracle as examples of enterprise systems sites will connect to.
claims.quote: enterprise systems such as SQL, SAP, and Oracle

claims.claim: The planned native support avoids building or maintaining custom integration layers.
claims.quote: without building or maintaining custom integration layers.

claims.claim: The roadmap highlights regulated and enterprise customers with data behind corporate firewalls.
claims.quote: This capability is especially valuable for regulated and enterprise customers such as banking and financial services, who need to surface data from systems hosted behind corporate firewalls.

claims.claim: General connector endpoint filtering controls allowed endpoints in the policy's targeted environments.
claims.quote: This opens a side panel where you specify an ordered list of Allow or Deny URL patterns. ... After you save your connector endpoint filtering rules and the data policy where they're defined, they are instantly enforced on the targeted environments.

claims.quote: Only static endpoints that are known and selected when building an app, flow, or chatbot during design time are enforced.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering is not enforced on dynamically bound runtime endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules aren't enforced on environment variables, custom inputs, and dynamically bound endpoints during runtime.

claims.claim: The Endpoint configurable column must be Yes for a connector to support endpoint filtering.
claims.quote: If the value of the Endpoint configurable column is Yes, you can use this capability by right-clicking and then selecting Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
